subtitle: Fire in the Monsoon Sky: Tipu Sultan’s Rockets and a Divided Legacy

panels.shot: low-angle dramatic wide of a battlefield night sky streaked with rising rockets arcing over distant British lines
panels.action: Tipu Sultan stands in war armour on the ramparts of Srirangapatna, one hand raised as iron-cased rockets roar into the dark monsoon sky above a distant East India Company camp.

dialogue.text: In Tipu Sultan’s age, iron rockets lit the Indian sky, shook the Company’s pride, and left a legacy as brilliant and as troubling as the fire he hurled into the night.

i18n.hi: टीपू के दौर में लोहे के रॉकेटों ने हिंदुस्तानी आसमान जला दिया, कंपनी का गुरूर हिला दिया, और उतनी ही चमकदार और बेचैन विरासत छोड़ी जितनी रात में उसकी आग थी।

panels.shot: slow push-in from aerial view of Mysore plateau towards Srirangapatna island-fort at dusk
panels.action: The island-fort of Srirangapatna glows with lamps along its walls as the Kaveri curves around; inside, Tipu Sultan, in simple court dress, studies plans by torchlight amid scrolls and weapons.

dialogue.text: To the British, Tipu Sultan was the ‘Tiger of Mysore’, a fearsome enemy. To his own court, he was also a restless experimenter, turning his river island capital into a workshop of war and rule.

i18n.hi: अँग्रेज़ों के लिए टीपू ‘मैसूर का शेर’ था, डरावना दुश्मन। अपनी दरबार में वह बेचैन तजुर्बेकार था, जिसने नदी-द्वीप राजधानी को जंग और हुकूमत की प्रयोगशाला बना दिया।

panels.shot: medium close-up over Tipu’s shoulder to a parchment sketch of rocket tubes and frames
panels.action: Tipu Sultan leans over a parchment showing careful drawings of iron cylinders strapped to bamboo poles beside ranks of infantry and cavalry in formation.

dialogue.text: Long before him, rockets had flared in Indian and other Asian skies. But Tipu, inheriting his father Hyder Ali’s ideas, forged them into disciplined brigades with iron cases, range and terror.

i18n.hi: उससे बहुत पहले भी भारत और एशिया के आसमानों में रॉकेट चमके थे। पर टीपू ने, बाप हैदर अली की सोच आगे बढ़ाकर, उन्हें लोहे की टुकड़ियों में ढाला—दूर तक मार, काबू और खौफ के साथ।

panels.shot: cutaway wide of a Mysore field workshop interior, lit by forge-fire
panels.action: Inside a Mysorean workshop, smiths hammer and shape glowing iron cylinders while others bind them to long bamboo sticks; rows of finished rockets lie stacked, orderly, on wooden racks.

dialogue.text: In the forges of Mysore, iron casings replaced fragile paper and bamboo. Stronger tubes carried more powder, flew farther and truer, and could be made by the hundreds under state control.

i18n.hi: मैसूर की भट्टियों में कागज़ और बाँस की नाज़ुक खोल हटकर लोहे ने जगह ली। मज़बूत नलियों ने ज़्यादा बारूद उठाया, दूर और सीधा उड़ीं, और सैकड़ों की तादाद में सरकारी कारखानों से निकलीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a training ground outside Srirangapatna with disciplined rocket corps arrayed
panels.action: On a dusty parade ground, rows of uniformed rocket-men kneel and stand in drilled precision as Tipu Sultan rides past on horseback, inspecting with an appraising, watchful gaze.

dialogue.text: Tipu did not leave rockets as curiosities. He folded them into his army, creating corps with ranks and officers, drilling them to launch salvos on signal, not in scattered village volleys.

i18n.hi: टीपू ने रॉकेटों को तमाशा नहीं रहने दिया। उन्हें फ़ौज में गूँथ दिया—अलग दस्ता, अपने अफ़सर, अभ्यास, और इशारे पर चलने वाली बरसात, न कि गाँवों की छिटपुट फायरिंग।

panels.shot: dynamic battlefield wide of Pollilur with arcing rockets over British square
panels.action: On an open plain near Pollilur, Company troops huddle in squares as a storm of rockets arcs overhead; some plunge into artillery lines, horses rear, and smoke rises in chaotic plumes.

dialogue.text: At battles like Pollilur, Mysore’s rockets tore through British lines, panicking men and beasts. Later, captured officers would admit they had never seen such sustained, directed rocket fire.

i18n.hi: पोलिलूर जैसी लड़ाइयों में मैसूर के रॉकेटों ने ब्रिटिश कतारें चीर डालीं, सिपाही और घोड़े दोनों दहशत में भागे। बाद में पकड़े गए अफ़सरों ने माना, इतनी लगातार, निशानेदार रॉकेट बारिश उन्होंने पहले कभी नहीं देखी।

panels.shot: close-up on Tipu’s face lit by rocket-flare on a night field
panels.action: Tipu Sultan stands on a rise at night, face half-lit by the reflected glow of rising rockets, eyes narrowed as he watches their paths across the sky.

dialogue.speaker: tipu_sultan
dialogue.text: Let their lines break before our steel must touch them.

i18n.hi: उनकी पंक्तियाँ यहीं टूट जाएँ, हमारे फ़ौलाद तक आने की नौबत ही न पड़े।

panels.shot: interior medium of Tipu at a low desk, writing by oil lamp with Persian scrolls around
panels.action: In a quiet chamber, Tipu Sultan writes a Persian letter, seals and coins on the desk beside him, a small model rocket lying among them like another instrument of state.

dialogue.text: His letters, later translated by Kirkpatrick, show a ruler who measured grain and gunpowder together. Rockets were tools in a wider design of revenues, reforms and relentless war.

i18n.hi: किर्कपैट्रिक की की हुई तरजुमा चिट्ठियाँ दिखाती हैं कि यह बादशाह गेहूँ और बारूद को साथ तोलता था। रॉकेट उसकी बड़ी नक़्शे वाली दुनिया में बस एक औज़ार थे—मालियात, सुधार और बेरहम जंग के साथ।

panels.shot: montage-style wide showing different administrative scenes separated by architectural arches
panels.action: Within a palace arcade, three arches frame scenes: Tipu examining new coin dies; officials debating at a calendar board; workers tending mulberry and silkworms under supervision, while Tipu stands overseeing from the center.

dialogue.text: He tinkered with coinage, adjusted calendars, carved new departments and pushed sericulture. His Mysore was both a battlefield and a laboratory, aimed at wealth and independence from Company control.

i18n.hi: वह सिक्के से खेलता, कैलेंडर बदलता, नए महकमे काटता और रेशम की खेती धकेलता रहा। उसका मैसूर एक साथ जंग का मैदान था और तजुर्बों की प्रयोगशाला—दौलत और कंपनी से आज़ादी, दोनों के लिए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Tipu in audience hall receiving envoys with a globe beside his throne
panels.action: Tipu Sultan sits on a modest but elevated throne, a small globe and maps at his side, as envoys bearing Ottoman and French fashions bow and present letters.

dialogue.text: From Srirangapatna, he reached out to Istanbul and Paris, seeking allies against the Company. His rockets and reforms were part of a larger gambit—to stand as an Indian power among empires.

i18n.hi: श्रीरंगपट्टन से वह इस्तांबुल और पेरिस तक हाथ बढ़ाता, कंपनी के खिलाफ़ हमसफ़र ढूँढता रहा। उसके रॉकेट और सुधार, एक बड़े दाँव का हिस्सा थे—साम्राज्यों के बीच एक हिंदुस्तानी ताकत बन खड़े होना।

panels.shot: somber wide of burned-out Malabar village with Mysore troops in background
panels.action: In a rain-drenched Malabar landscape, a blackened temple gopuram and smoldering houses stand silent as Mysore soldiers march away; Tipu Sultan watches from horseback, his expression unreadable amid the smoke.

dialogue.text: Yet the same state that forged rockets also pressed its rule harshly. In Coorg and Malabar, sources speak of coercion, forced conversions and uprooted communities under Tipu’s campaigns.

i18n.hi: पर वही रियासत जो रॉकेट ढालती थी, हुकूमत भी सख़्ती से थोपती थी। कूर्ग और मलाबार में स्रोत ज़बरदस्ती, मज़हबी दबाव और उजड़ी बस्तियों की बातें करते हैं, टीपू की चढ़ाइयों के नाम पर।

panels.shot: tight close-up of Tipu’s hand holding prayer beads over a campaign map marked with crosses and crescents
panels.action: Tipu’s hand, holding a string of beads, rests on a map showing hills, forts and coastal towns, some marked with crescents, others with small temple towers and churches sketched by scribes.

dialogue.text: Some letters show him as a patron of shrines and mosques; others boast of bringing ‘infidels’ to the faith. The record refuses a simple hero or villain, even as legend demands one.

i18n.hi: कुछ खत उसे मज़ारों और मस्जिदों का सरपरस्त दिखाते हैं; और कुछ ‘काफ़िरों’ को ईमान पर लाने पर फख्र करते हैं। दस्तावेज़ साफ़-साफ़ न हीरो मानते हैं न खलनायक, जबकि क़िस्से किसी एक की माँग करते हैं।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of Srirangapatna under siege with British lines and batteries encircling
panels.action: From above, Srirangapatna’s walls bristle with defenders as British siege lines and artillery batteries encircle the island; smoke rises where shots land, and thin trails of rockets launch from within the fort.

dialogue.text: In 1799, the Company returned with allies and heavy guns. Rockets, so shocking in open battle, could not by themselves break a tightening siege around Srirangapatna’s stone and mud.

i18n.hi: १७९९ में कंपनी फिर लौटी—हमसफ़रों और भारी तोपों के साथ। खुले मैदान में दहशत बन चुके रॉकेट, अकेले, श्रीरंगपट्टन की पत्थर-मिट्टी की दीवारों पर कसती घेराबंदी नहीं तोड़ सके।

panels.shot: medium shot on the ramparts as Tipu confers with officers amid incoming fire
panels.action: On the battered ramparts, Tipu Sultan, armour dented and turban askew, confers with anxious officers as enemy shells burst in the distance; a rack of unused rockets stands nearby.

dialogue.speaker: tipu_sultan
dialogue.text: If we must fall, let it be on these walls, not at their feet.

i18n.hi: अगर गिरना है, तो इन दीवारों पर गिरें, उनके पैरों पर नहीं।

panels.shot: melancholic interior wide of British officers examining captured rockets after the fall
panels.action: Inside a captured armoury, British officers in red coats bend over piles of Mysorean rockets, measuring iron tubes and sketching them while Indian artisans stand aside, watching quietly.

dialogue.text: When the fort fell, not just jewels and manuscripts were taken. Hundreds of iron rockets crossed the seas, studied and reshaped into Congreve rockets that would later blaze over European wars.

i18n.hi: किले के गिरते ही सिर्फ़ जेवर और पांडुलिपियाँ नहीं उठीं। सैकड़ों लोहे के रॉकेट समंदर पार ले जाए गए, परखे गए और ढलकर कॉन्ग्रीव रॉकेट बने, जो बाद में यूरोपी जंगों के आसमान पर जले।

panels.shot: split-screen style wide: on one side a British Congreve rocket launch, on the other a Mysore rocket brigade training
panels.action: On one half, British gunners fire Congreve rockets over a European battlefield; on the other, Mysore rocketeers in earlier years launch their iron-cased weapons from wicker frames in a dusty Indian field.

dialogue.text: Later admirers would hail Tipu as the father of war rockets. The truth is quieter: his state refined and scaled an older craft so powerfully that distant empires rebuilt his designs for their own wars.

i18n.hi: बाद के मुरीदों ने टीपू को जंगी रॉकेटों का बाप कहा। सच्चाई कुछ धीमी है—उसकी रियासत ने पुरानी हुनर को इतना निखारा और फैलाया कि दूर के साम्राज्यों ने अपनी जंगों के लिए उसी की बनावटें दोहराईं।

panels.shot: introspective medium close-up of Tipu’s statue or portrait being cleaned in a modern museum gallery
panels.action: In a modern gallery, a conservator carefully wipes dust from a portrait of Tipu Sultan; behind, a display case holds surviving iron rockets, their dark metal scarred but intact.

dialogue.text: Today, Tipu’s name sparks praise and protest. In museums, his rockets lie between these arguments—mute steel that carries both resistance to empire and the weight of those he ruled harshly.

i18n.hi: आज टीपू का नाम तारीफ़ और तकरार दोनों जगाता है। म्यूज़ियमों में उसके रॉकेट इन बहसों के बीच रखे हैं—खामोश लोहा, जो एक तरफ़ साम्राज्य के ख़िलाफ़ बगावत, और दूसरी तरफ़ उसके सख़्त राज का बोझ उठाए है।

panels.shot: final wide of a twilight sky over Srirangapatna with a single ceremonial rocket rising
panels.action: Over the twilight silhouette of Srirangapatna’s walls and temple towers, a single ceremonial rocket climbs, leaving a glowing trail before fading into the darkening sky.

dialogue.text: To face Tipu’s story is to stand under that fading trail: to see ingenuity and oppression together, and to learn to tell our past without dimming either the fire of achievement or the shadows it cast.

i18n.hi: टीपू की कहानी का सामना करना, उस मुरझाती रॉकेट लकीर के नीचे खड़े होना है—जहाँ हुनर और ज़ुल्म साथ दिखते हैं, और जहाँ हमें अतीत यूँ कहना सीखना है कि न कारनामों की आग फीकी पड़े, न उसके डाले साए।
